skill.name: agy-worker
skill.description: Delegate approved repository exploration and implementation to Google Antigravity CLI while Codex reviews diffs, verifies results, and manages bounded repair cycles.
skill.summary: Coordinate AGY repository work with isolated worktrees, review gates, and bounded verification cycles.
skill.author: cagdasyurekli

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, minified JSON Schemas, defensive control-character checks, and fixed argv subprocesses. Confirmed risks include external AGY dispatch, unrestricted driver-supplied Bash verification, and inherited environment exposure. The skill also embeds system-style persona prompts and intentionally transmits approved repository content to Google or Gemini services. Static review was capped at 400/724 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 324 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: AGY processes inherit the complete controller environment.
remediation.suggestion: Build an allowlisted child environment containing only documented AGY requirements, locale settings, and explicitly approved authentication variables.

remediation.issue: Verification accepts free-form shell command strings with ambient credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer structured argv commands, run checks with a minimal environment, and require explicit confirmation before commands needing secrets or network access.

remediation.issue: Persona files present task prompts as system instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Represent personas as bounded task context, remove system-authority labels, and delimit repository content so it cannot redefine persona rules.

remediation.issue: Repository content is transmitted to an external provider.
remediation.suggestion: Keep exact-scope consent mandatory, show the resolved readable paths, and support a dry-run manifest before provider launch.

semantic_findings.title: Embedded System-Style Persona Instructions
semantic_findings.description: Three persona files label their content "Agent System Instructions" and direct downstream agents with "You are" role commands. These prompts can steer model behavior when dispatched.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly identify the text as system instructions and immediately assign roles to a downstream agent. The behavior is intentional, but the system-style authority is unambiguous.

semantic_findings.title: External Provider Receives Approved Repository Content
semantic_findings.description: The workflow intentionally sends task and readable repository content to Google or Gemini services after user approval. Incorrect scope approval can disclose proprietary source.

content.value_statement: Large repository tasks require exploration, implementation, and verification across many files. This skill delegates approved work to AGY and keeps Codex responsible for review.
actual_capabilities: Dispatches exploration, bounded tasks, and project workflows to the AGY command-line tool.
Creates isolated, branch-backed worktrees for repository editing workflows.
Tracks provider jobs through start, status, wait, continue, finalize, cancel, and restart operations.
Validates worker result envelopes and binds lifecycle actions to state and candidate hashes.
Supports driver-owned verification commands, diff review, repair cycles, and evidence receipts.
Provides model selection checks, compatibility probes, diagnostics, benchmarks, and usage reports.
limitations: Requires a compatible AGY installation and access to Google or Gemini services.
Repository content leaves the local machine only after explicit provider transmission approval.
Verification can execute driver-supplied shell commands with local filesystem and environment access.
Offline checks cannot prove provider availability, authentication, or complete implementation quality.

use_cases.title: Survey an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Generate a bounded architecture and test-command inventory before planning changes.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers onboarding to an existing codebase

use_cases.title: Implement a repository feature
use_cases.description: Delegate edits in an isolated worktree, then review and verify the resulting candidate.

use_cases.title: Audit and repair a project
use_cases.description: Run broader implementation cycles with independent review, targeted checks, and bounded continuation feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore this approved repository. Map entry points, architecture, dependencies, test commands, and risky areas. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a bounded task
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the requested change in the isolated worktree. Keep scope focused, list changed files, and leave verification to Codex.

prompt_templates.title: Backfill targeted tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Add tests for the specified behavior using existing conventions. Change test files only and report any production-code blocker.

prompt_templates.title: Run a reviewed project cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and implement this project request. Preserve authority boundaries, acceptance criteria, and privacy constraints for independent Codex review.

output_examples.input: Explore the repository and identify its main test commands.
output_examples.output: Repository survey covering entry points, important directories, dependencies, verified test commands, risky areas, and unexamined paths.

output_examples.input: Add validation for empty configuration values and update tests.
output: Candidate changes isolated in a branch-backed worktree.
Diff review findings and driver-owned verification results.
Final assurance marked verified, partially verified, rejected, or blocked.

output_examples.input: Audit and repair the project within five cycles.
output_examples.output: A reviewed candidate with bounded repair history, evidence gaps, check outcomes, and an explicit final disposition.

best_practices: Approve the exact repository scope before any provider dispatch.
Use isolated worktrees and inspect every candidate diff before acceptance.
Run trusted, driver-selected checks and report missing or failed verification honestly.
anti_patterns: Do not send credentials, unrelated files, raw logs, or controller state to AGY.
Do not execute commands or test claims returned by the worker envelope.
Do not commit, push, publish, install, or submit feedback without separate approval.

faq.question: What is AGY in this skill?
faq.answer: AGY is the Google Antigravity command-line tool used as an external repository worker.

faq.question: Does the skill modify my main checkout?
faq.answer: Editing workflows use a disposable branch-backed worktree. Codex reviews the candidate before any separate integration action.

faq.question: Is repository content sent externally?
faq.answer: Yes. AGY uses Google or Gemini services, so the skill requires explicit approval for the exact readable repository scope.

faq.question: Who runs tests and build checks?
faq.answer: Codex selects and runs verification. Worker-provided command claims are rejected and never treated as evidence.

faq.question: Can the skill commit or push changes?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Commits, pushes, pull requests, publishing, installations, and feedback submissions require separate approval.

faq.question: What happens when verification fails?
faq.answer: Codex can request a bounded continuation while cycles remain, or finalize with a partial, rejected, or blocked disposition.
